topic: Non-standard consumer device edge cases for WakePoint (Flutter Android transit wake-up alarm), 2026 / Android 15–16
headline: Core local-alarm loop survives almost everywhere (GPS + local FGS + local notification need no Google services), but Google Maps, FCM push, Ads and Play Billing all hard-break on no-GMS devices; the real threats to "fire on time with screen off for 2h" are OEM battery-killers and Android Go LMK on 2GB phones, not the exotic device types.

version_matrix.mechanism: Foreground service TYPE is mandatory — startForeground() throws MissingForegroundServiceTypeException/SecurityException if the running service's android:foregroundServiceType and matching FOREGROUND_SERVICE_* permission are not both declared
version_matrix.behavior: WakePoint's flutter_background_service already declares foregroundServiceType="location|mediaPlayback" and both FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK perms — this is correct. The location type ALSO requires ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION granted before startForeground, or it is rejected.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Guard: only call the location FGS after ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is granted (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT>=34). Keep the manifest service type = location|mediaPlayback. If GPS/location perm is ever revoked at runtime, the FGS can be force-stopped by the system — catch and re-prompt.

version_matrix.mechanism: Restrictions on starting a foreground service from the background; the SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW exemption narrowed — an app now needs a currently-VISIBLE TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY window, not just the permission, to start an FGS from background
version_matrix.behavior: If WakePoint tries to (re)start its location FGS from a background/killed state (e.g. after an OEM kill) it will throw ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException unless it has a qualifying exemption (battery-optimization-exempt, or a visible overlay, or user just interacted).
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Start the FGS while the Activity is foreground (at ride-arm time), not lazily from background. Request REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS (this exemption still lets an exempt app start FGS from bg). Do not rely on SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW alone on API>=35. Test with: adb shell am compat enable FGS_SAW_RESTRICTIONS <pkg>.

version_matrix.mechanism: Motion/position sensor sampling rate capped at 200 Hz unless HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS is declared; if the user's mic toggle is OFF, sensors are ALWAYS rate-limited regardless of the permission
version_matrix.behavior: WakePoint targets 50–100 Hz, which is UNDER the 200 Hz cap, so the permission is not strictly required — but the manifest already declares HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS (harmless, future-proof). Real risk: if the device mic toggle is off, delivery may drop below requested rate.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Keep the permission (harmless). Do not assume the OS honors your requested Hz — measure actual inter-sample delta in the isolate and adapt the EKF timestep to real dt rather than nominal 50/100 Hz. Never hard-require >100 Hz.

version_matrix.mechanism: Devices with <=2 GB RAM must return ActivityManager.isLowRamDevice()==true and ship as Android (Go edition); Go applies extra background limits and a far more aggressive LowMemoryKiller
version_matrix.api_level: Android 11+ (API 30) for the 2GB mandate; isLowRamDevice available since API 19
version_matrix.behavior: An FGS is initially shielded from LMK but is NOT immune — under sustained pressure the system will kill even a location FGS. A 2h screen-off run on a 2GB Go device is the single biggest reliability risk after OEM killers.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: At runtime read isLowRamDevice(): if true, drop sensor rate to 50 Hz, evict map tiles/heavy UI from memory while backgrounded, keep the background isolate RSS minimal, and lean harder on GPS-only geofence checks. Hold a partial WakeLock + battery-optimization exemption. Treat Go as DEGRADED, not guaranteed.

version_matrix.mechanism: USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT: fresh installs no longer get the full-screen-intent capability auto-granted; only apps whose core function is alarm or calling are eligible, and Play requires a declaration
version_matrix.behavior: WakePoint's guaranteed audible/visual wake screen relies on a full-screen intent notification. On API>=34 this is granted by default ONLY because an alarm app qualifies; otherwise the notification demotes to a heads-up banner and will NOT wake a sleeping rider with screen off.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Keep USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT in the manifest. On API>=34 check NotificationManager.canUseFullScreenIntent(); if false, deep-link the user to the FSI settings toggle. Declare the alarm use-case in Play Console. Do not depend solely on FSI — also start an Activity with showWhenLocked/turnScreenOn (already set) + audio FGS as belt-and-suspenders.

version_matrix.mechanism: geolocator resolves the location engine at runtime: FusedLocationProviderClient when Google Play Services is present, else automatic fallback to the platform LocationManager (raw GPS/GNSS)
version_matrix.api_level: Package behavior (geolocator ^14), not an OS API level — applies on all no-GMS devices
version_matrix.behavior: On Huawei/HMS and other no-GMS devices, location still works via LocationManager, but you lose fused Wi-Fi/cell-assisted fixes, faster TTFF, and the fused dead-reckoning that helps in metro tunnels. Accuracy/battery are worse and cold-fix is slower.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Do NOT set forceAndroidLocationManager blindly (known null-fix bugs when GMS present). Let geolocator auto-select. Because fused tunnel assistance is absent on no-GMS, WakePoint's own accel/EKF dead-reckoning becomes the primary in-tunnel signal — make the EKF the source of truth between GPS fixes, not an add-on.

device_class_requirements.requirements: CORE ALARM WORKS: geolocator falls back to LocationManager (raw GPS), local FGS runs, flutter_local_notifications fires locally, sensors_plus works — none need Google services. BROKEN: google_maps_flutter renders a blank/grey map or crashes (needs GMS Maps) → must fall back to flutter_map/OSM (project already bundles assets/osm/, so wire that path for GMS-absent devices). BROKEN: FCM push (no remote wake — but the alarm is LOCAL so this is non-fatal; only remote config/marketing is lost). BROKEN: google_mobile_ads and in_app_purchase/Play Billing require Play Store → no monetization on AppGallery. DEGRADED: no fused Wi-Fi/cell location, worse tunnel fixes → lean on EKF. Solo-founder verdict: do NOT integrate the HMS SDK stack (Location/Map/Push Kit + AppGallery listing) — Huawei's no-GMS share in India is tiny and shrinking. Instead: detect GMS at runtime (GoogleApiAvailability / try google_maps_flutter and catch), auto-switch to OSM map, keep local alarm, and hide Ads/IAP gracefully.

device_class_requirements.device_class: Android Go edition / <=2-3 GB RAM budget phones (the India core market)
device_class_requirements.requirements: FGS is shielded from LMK only initially; a 2h screen-off run can still be killed under memory pressure — this plus OEM killers is the top reliability risk. Requirements: read ActivityManager.isLowRamDevice() and, when true, cut sensor rate to 50 Hz, evict map tiles and heavy widgets from RAM while backgrounded, keep the background isolate footprint minimal; hold a partial WakeLock; obtain REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS exemption; keep the ongoing FGS notification visible. Add a watchdog: persist ride state to Hive and, if the isolate is respawned after a kill, immediately re-arm. Treat as best-effort, warn power-users to whitelist the app.

Config-change safe: the Activity already lists screenSize|smallestScreenSize|screenLayout|density|uiMode|orientation|locale|layoutDirection|fontScale in configChanges, so fold/unfold/rotate will NOT recreate the Activity or interrupt the background isolate — good. Two gaps: (a) many Wi-Fi-only tablets have NO GPS — check PackageManager.hasSystemFeature(FEATURE_LOCATION_GPS) and block/warn if absent (UNSUPPORTED without GPS); (b) build a responsive layout for large screens (Play large-screen quality). Foldable posture changes are handled by the configChanges flags; verify the map/list reflows.

device_class_requirements.device_class: Phones with NO gyroscope / low-quality accelerometer (very common on budget India devices)
device_class_requirements.requirements: Gyroscope must be OPTIONAL. sensors_plus gyroscopeEventStream will error or never emit on gyro-less devices — guard by checking SensorManager.getDefaultSensor(TYPE_GYROSCOPE)==null (or catch the stream error) at startup. WakePoint's motion/arrival logic must run on accelerometer + GPS alone; the EKF should degrade to an accel-only mode (no gyro orientation term) rather than failing. For noisy cheap accelerometers, apply low-pass filtering and rely on GPS as the absolute-position corrector so bad IMU data cannot cause a false/late alarm. Never gate ride-arming on gyro presence.

device_class_requirements.device_class: China-market ROMs with no Google at all (e.g. domestic Xiaomi/Oppo/Vivo China builds)
device_class_requirements.requirements: Out of scope for an India-first launch — do not invest. Same GMS breakage as Huawei PLUS Google endpoints (Maps tiles, Places REST, FCM) are network-blocked in China, and OSM tiles may be throttled. Core local alarm + LocationManager GPS could still function if the user sideloads, but maps/autocomplete will fail. If you ever target China you'd need a domestic tile/map provider (Amap/AutoNavi) and a China push channel — a separate product. Default stance: detect and show a clear 'maps unavailable in this region' fallback, keep local alarm running.

Add android:supportsRtl="true" to the <application> tag (currently MISSING) so native views mirror for Urdu/RTL users. In Flutter, wire MaterialApp localizationsDelegates + supportedLocales and let Directionality follow the locale (manifest already keeps locale|layoutDirection in configChanges, so switching language won't recreate the Activity). Format all clock times through intl and honor MediaQuery.alwaysUse24HourFormat — India mixes 12h phone UI with 24h rail timetables, so never hardcode either. Localize the arrival/ETA strings and numerals (Devanagari digits where appropriate).

Essentially a non-issue: GPS and the local alarm need no SIM or telephony. Do NOT request READ_PHONE_STATE or assume a cellular network. Only caveat: on a no-SIM device there is no cell-tower-assisted location, so cold-fix and tunnel fallback are slightly worse — mitigated by the EKF and by allowing Wi-Fi. Ensure map/Places calls tolerate Wi-Fi-only connectivity (connectivity_plus already present). Dual-SIM/eSIM require zero special handling.

wakepoint_actions: Add a single runtime GMS-availability probe (GoogleApiAvailability.isGooglePlayServicesAvailable or a caught google_maps_flutter init) and branch: GMS present → Google Map; absent → flutter_map/OSM using the already-bundled assets/osm/ tiles. This one switch covers Huawei, no-GMS, and China map breakage.

Make the accel/EKF the primary between-fix position source, not a supplement — this is what keeps arrivals accurate in metro tunnels AND on no-GMS phones that lack fused dead-reckoning. Gate NOTHING on gyroscope: detect TYPE_GYROSCOPE==null and run an accel-only EKF mode.

Harden against LMK + OEM killers (the real 2h-screen-off threats): request REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS, hold a partial WakeLock, keep the FGS notification visible, persist ride state to Hive, and add a respawn-and-re-arm watchdog. Read isLowRamDevice() and downshift sensor rate + memory on Go devices. Ship a dontkillmyapp-style per-OEM (Xiaomi/MIUI autostart, Oppo/Vivo/Realme) whitelist walkthrough in onboarding.

Protect the wake mechanism on API>=34: keep USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT, check NotificationManager.canUseFullScreenIntent() and deep-link to its toggle if denied, declare the alarm use-case in Play Console, and keep showWhenLocked/turnScreenOn + an audio (mediaPlayback) FGS as redundant wake paths so a demoted notification never silently fails.

Guard the location FGS start: only startForeground after ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is granted, and start it while the Activity is foreground (not from a background/killed state) to avoid the Android 15 ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException; rely on the battery-optimization exemption for post-kill restarts.

Treat monetization as GMS-only: wrap google_mobile_ads and in_app_purchase so their absence on no-GMS devices degrades silently rather than crashing the core alarm. Do not build HMS/AppGallery support as a solo founder — the ROI for India is not there.

Fix locale/RTL gaps: add android:supportsRtl="true" to <application>, add Flutter localization delegates, and format every time via intl honoring alwaysUse24HourFormat. Do not require SIM/telephony permissions — dual-SIM/eSIM/no-SIM need no special code.

Resolve the build-config conflict noted in the brief: having both build.gradle and build.gradle.kts is undefined behavior — pick one (Gradle uses .kts if present) and delete the other before shipping, and confirm minSdk explicitly (Flutter default may be too low for the FGS-type and sensor guards above).

## WakePoint — Non-standard consumer device edge cases (2026 / Android 15–16)

**Bottom line:** WakePoint's *core value loop* — GPS tracking + a location foreground service + a locally-scheduled full-screen audible alarm — depends on **zero Google services** and therefore survives on almost every device class, including no-GMS phones. What breaks on the edges is the *Google-branded surface*: Google Maps rendering, FCM push, AdMob, and Play Billing. The genuine threats to "fire on time, screen off, 2 hours" are **OEM battery-killers (Xiaomi/Oppo/Vivo/Realme)** and the **Android Go LowMemoryKiller on 2 GB phones** — i.e. the *mainstream cheap India phone*, not the exotic device.

I verified the current manifest and pubspec. Good news already in place: `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION` + `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK` perms, `foregroundServiceType="location|mediaPlayback"`, `HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS`, `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT`, `showWhenLocked`/`turnScreenOn`, a broad `configChanges` list, and bundled `assets/osm/` tiles. Gaps and per-class actions below.

Manifest: `/home/raed/Projects/WakePoint/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
Pubspec: `/home/raed/Projects/WakePoint/pubspec.yaml`

---

### (1) No-GMS Huawei / Honor (HMS) — **DEGRADED**
- **Location — WORKS (degraded):** `geolocator ^14` auto-falls back from `FusedLocationProviderClient` to the platform `LocationManager` (raw GNSS) when Play Services is absent. You lose Wi-Fi/cell-assisted fixes, fast TTFF, and fused tunnel dead-reckoning. Do **not** force `forceAndroidLocationManager` (known null-fix bug when GMS *is* present).
- **Maps — BROKEN:** `google_maps_flutter` shows a blank/grey map or crashes without GMS. Fall back to `flutter_map`/OSM (you already ship `assets/osm/`). Huawei Map Kit exists but is not worth a solo founder's time.
- **Places autocomplete — WORKS:** `google_places_flutter` uses the Places **REST** API over HTTPS — not GMS-dependent (needs only an API key + internet + billing enabled).
- **Push — BROKEN but non-fatal:** FCM needs GMS. The alarm is *local*, so no remote wake is required; only remote config/marketing is lost.
- **Ads + IAP — BROKEN:** `google_mobile_ads` and `in_app_purchase` (Play Billing) require the Play Store → no monetization on AppGallery.
- **Solo-founder call:** Skip the whole HMS SDK path. Huawei's no-GMS footprint in India is small and shrinking. Just detect GMS absence at runtime and degrade (OSM map, hidden ads/IAP, local alarm).

### (2) Android Go / ≤2–3 GB RAM (the India core market) — **DEGRADED**
- Devices with ≤2 GB **must** return `isLowRamDevice()==true` (Android 11+ mandate) and get Go's extra background limits + aggressive LMK. An FGS is shielded *initially* but **not immune** — a 2 h screen-off run can be killed.
- **Do:** read `isLowRamDevice()` → drop sensors to 50 Hz, evict map tiles/heavy UI from RAM while backgrounded, keep the isolate lean; hold a partial `WakeLock`; get `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS`; persist ride state to Hive and re-arm on isolate respawn. This is best-effort, not guaranteed.

### (3) Tablets & foldables — **WITH_SETUP**
- Config-change safe already (`screenSize|smallestScreenSize|screenLayout|density|uiMode|orientation|locale|layoutDirection|fontScale` in `configChanges`) → fold/unfold/rotate won't recreate the Activity or interrupt the isolate.
- **Gaps:** many Wi-Fi-only tablets have **no GPS** → check `hasSystemFeature(FEATURE_LOCATION_GPS)` and block/warn (UNSUPPORTED without GPS). Add a responsive large-screen layout (Play large-screen quality).

### (4) No gyroscope / low-quality accelerometer (very common on budget India phones) — **WITH_SETUP**
- Make gyro **optional**: `sensors_plus` gyro stream errors/never emits on gyro-less devices — guard with `getDefaultSensor(TYPE_GYROSCOPE)==null` (or catch the stream error). Run an **accel-only EKF mode**; use GPS as the absolute-position corrector so noisy cheap IMUs can't cause a false/late alarm. Never gate ride-arming on gyro presence.

### (5) China-market ROMs, no Google at all — **UNSUPPORTED (out of scope)**
- Same GMS breakage as Huawei *plus* Google endpoints (Maps, Places REST, FCM) are network-blocked and OSM tiles may be throttled. Local alarm + LocationManager GPS could still run if sideloaded, but maps/autocomplete fail. Don't invest for an India-first launch; show a clear regional fallback.

### (6) Region / RTL / locale / 12-24h — **WITH_SETUP**
- **Add `android:supportsRtl="true"`** to `<application>` (currently missing) for Urdu/RTL mirroring of native views. Wire Flutter `localizationsDelegates` + `supportedLocales`; the manifest's `locale|layoutDirection` in `configChanges` means language switches won't recreate the Activity. Format all times through `intl`, honoring `MediaQuery.alwaysUse24HourFormat` — India mixes 12 h phone UI with 24 h rail timetables, so never hardcode.

### (7) Dual-SIM / eSIM / no-SIM (data-only) — **FULLY**
- Non-issue. GPS + local alarm need no SIM/telephony — don't request `READ_PHONE_STATE`. Only caveat: no-SIM loses cell-assisted location (slightly worse cold fix/tunnel fallback), covered by the EKF + Wi-Fi. Dual-SIM/eSIM need zero special handling.

---

### Cross-cutting reliability note (applies to all classes)
The dominant real-world failure mode in India is **OEM power management** (MIUI autostart/background limits, Oppo/Vivo/Realme killers) plus **Go-device LMK** — not the device *type*. Mitigate with: battery-optimization exemption, visible FGS notification, WakeLock, Hive-persisted state + respawn watchdog, and a per-OEM whitelist walkthrough in onboarding (dontkillmyapp.com guides).

### Housekeeping flagged by the brief
Both `build.gradle` and `build.gradle.kts` present is undefined — Gradle prefers `.kts` if it exists; pick one, delete the other, and confirm an explicit `minSdk` (Flutter's default may be too low for the API-level guards above) before shipping.

**Facts marked HARD FACT** are the cited API-level behavior changes in the version matrix (FGS types API 34, bg-FGS/SAW API 35, sensor 200 Hz cap API 31, isLowRamDevice mandate API 30, FSI restriction API 34, geolocator fallback = documented package behavior). Everything about *whether a given cheap phone kills your service* is **INFERENCE** — it is OEM- and firmware-specific and must be validated on real hardware.

Sources: [FGS types required (API 34)](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/14/changes/fgs-types-required) · [Restrictions on bg FGS start / SAW (API 35)](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/restrictions-bg-start) · [Android 15 behavior changes](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-15) · [Sensors overview / 200 Hz cap (API 31)](https://developer.android.com/develop/sensors-and-location/sensors/sensors_overview) · [Android Go develop guide](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/androidgo/develop) · [Memory management](https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/memory-management) · [Full-screen intent policy](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13392821) · [geolocator (fused→LocationManager fallback)](https://pub.dev/packages/geolocator) · [google_maps_flutter needs GMS (flutter#85787)](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/85787) · [Don't kill my app!](https://dontkillmyapp.com/)

topic: Correct SDK config (min/target/compile SDK, Java, Kotlin, NDK) and Google Play 2026 compliance for the WakePoint Flutter location+alarm app
headline: Ship compileSdk 36 / targetSdk 36 / minSdk 24 / Java 11 + desugaring / NDK r28; the active build.gradle's targetSdk 34 is already Play-non-compliant and the duplicate .kts files are dead code that must be deleted.

version_matrix.mechanism: Google Play target API level requirement — new apps & updates (current, in force)
version_matrix.behavior: Since 31 Aug 2025, every NEW app and every app UPDATE submitted to Play must targetSdk >= 35 or the Play Console rejects the upload. WakePoint's ACTIVE config (android/app/build.gradle) is targetSdk 34 — this is ALREADY rejected today (Jul 2026).
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Raise targetSdk from 34 to at least 35 immediately; go straight to 36 (see next row). This is the single most urgent fix.

version_matrix.mechanism: Google Play target API level requirement — next bump (imminent)
version_matrix.behavior: From 31 Aug 2026 (~7 weeks out), new apps and updates must targetSdk 36; existing apps must be >=35 to stay discoverable to new users on Android 16/17 devices. One-time extension requestable to 1 Nov 2026. Wear/TV/Auto are one level behind.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Set compileSdk 36 and targetSdk 36 now so a single build survives both the current rule and the 31 Aug 2026 deadline without a second migration.

version_matrix.mechanism: 16 KB memory page-size support for native (.so) libraries
version_matrix.behavior: Since 1 Nov 2025, new apps/updates targeting API 35+ must ship 64-bit native libraries aligned to 16 KB ELF pages or they crash/are rejected on 16 KB-page devices (Pixel 8+/flagships on Android 15+). NDK r28+ compiles 16 KB-aligned by default.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Keep ndkVersion r28 (already 28.2.13676358) and AGP 8.5.1+; rebuild after upgrading every native plugin (sensors_plus, geolocator, google_maps_flutter, google_mobile_ads, vibration, connectivity_plus) to a 16 KB-aligned release; verify with `zipalign -c -P 16` / check-elf-alignment on the AAB.

version_matrix.mechanism: Edge-to-edge display enforcement
version_matrix.behavior: targetSdk 35 forces the window behind the system bars; you may opt out via android:windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement=true. At targetSdk 36 that attribute is deprecated/ignored — edge-to-edge is mandatory, so content can render under the status/nav bars.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Because you go to targetSdk 36, do NOT rely on opt-out. Wrap Flutter UI in SafeArea and apply SystemChrome.setSystemUIOverlayStyle so the full-screen alarm and map controls are not hidden behind system bars.

version_matrix.mechanism: Foreground service types required + Play FGS declaration
version_matrix.behavior: Apps targeting 34+ must declare a foregroundServiceType for every FGS and hold the matching permission, or the service throws at startForeground(). location and mediaPlayback are already declared in the manifest. Play also requires a Foreground Service declaration in Play Console App Content justifying the 'location' type for a 2h screen-off use case.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Keep FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK permissions and the service's foregroundServiceType='location|mediaPlayback'; file the Play Console FGS declaration with a video showing the transit wake-up flow.

version_matrix.mechanism: Exact-alarm permission gating + Play restricted-permission policy
version_matrix.behavior: For targetSdk 33+, SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is NOT auto-granted; USE_EXACT_ALARM (auto-granted, API 33+) is a Play-restricted permission allowed ONLY for genuine alarm/timer/calendar apps. WakePoint qualifies as an alarm app, but the manifest currently declares NEITHER exact-alarm permission.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Add USE_EXACT_ALARM (core alarm functionality) and submit the Play restricted-permission declaration with a demo video; do not rely on inexact alarms for the final wake-up trigger. Declaring it works on API 33+ and is harmlessly ignored below 33.

version_matrix.mechanism: POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission
version_matrix.behavior: On API 33+ the foreground-service notification (and alarm notification) requires the user to grant POST_NOTIFICATIONS at runtime; denied means no visible FGS notification. Permission is declared but only prompts on 33+.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Request POST_NOTIFICATIONS at runtime (permission_handler) guarded by Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33; keep the manifest declaration. No minSdk impact.

version_matrix.mechanism: google_mobile_ads (Google Mobile Ads SDK v24) minimum SDK floor
version_matrix.behavior: GMA SDK 24.0.0 (Feb 2025), wrapped by google_mobile_ads ^6.0.0, requires minSdk >= 23 or the manifest merger fails. This is the highest minSdk floor among WakePoint's plugins (maps/in_app_purchase/geolocator sit at 21).
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: minSdk cannot go below 23 while AdMob is included. Set minSdk 24 (only ~0.4% extra reach cost over 23) for a clean modern floor, or 23 to squeeze the last fraction.

version_matrix.mechanism: Background location separate grant (India cheap-phone reality)
version_matrix.behavior: From targetSdk 30, ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION cannot be requested in the same prompt as foreground location — the user must pick 'Allow all the time' from a separate Settings screen. Play requires a Location Permissions declaration justifying background use.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Two-step runtime request (foreground first, then background via Settings deep-link); file the Play background-location declaration. Consider whether a foreground-only FGS 'location' with the service started while app is open avoids needing background location at all.

version_matrix.mechanism: Duplicate build.gradle vs build.gradle.kts precedence
version_matrix.behavior: When both a Groovy build.gradle and a Kotlin build.gradle.kts exist in the SAME directory, Gradle uses the Groovy build.gradle and silently ignores the .kts. So the ACTIVE config is the Groovy files (compileSdk 36, targetSdk 34, Java 8); the .kts files (Java 11, flutter.* SDK values) are dead code and a maintenance trap.
version_matrix.what_wakepoint_must_do: Delete android/build.gradle.kts and android/app/build.gradle.kts (project is Groovy — settings.gradle is Groovy-only). Then fix the surviving Groovy android/app/build.gradle values.

device_class_requirements.requirements: With compileSdk/targetSdk 36, minSdk 24, correct FGS + exact-alarm + notification permissions, and a battery-optimization exemption prompt. This is the primary target and the 2h screen-off alarm is reliable here.

device_class_requirements.device_class: Aggressive-OEM phones (Xiaomi MIUI/HyperOS, Oppo/Vivo/Realme ColorOS, Samsung OneUI, Transsion) — dominant in India
device_class_requirements.requirements: Foreground service + wakelock survive only if the user grants Autostart and sets battery usage to 'Unrestricted/No restrictions'. WakePoint must detect OEM (device_info_plus) and deep-link the user to the per-OEM autostart/battery screen (android_intent_plus) during onboarding, plus request REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS. Without this the service is killed well before 2h.

device_class_requirements.device_class: Android Go / low-RAM (2GB, Android 11–15) budget India phones
device_class_requirements.requirements: 50–100Hz accel/gyro streaming + wakelock + FGS is heavy; the OS kills low-priority services under memory pressure. Needs battery-optimization exemption, a persistent high-importance FGS notification, and ideally a lower sensor rate fallback. HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS (API 31+) is declared and required for >200Hz but 50–100Hz is fine without it.

Every bundled native .so (Flutter engine + sensors_plus, geolocator, maps, ads, vibration) must be 16 KB-aligned. Guaranteed only after building with NDK r28+ (already set) and updating all native plugins to 16 KB-compliant releases; otherwise the app crashes on launch on these devices and is blocked at Play upload for targetSdk 35+.

device_class_requirements.device_class: No-GMS / AOSP phones (some India budget SKUs, Huawei, de-Googled)
device_class_requirements.requirements: Core wake-up path (AlarmManager exact alarm, sensors_plus, FGS 'location', audible alarm, vibration) works. But google_mobile_ads, google_maps_flutter, google_places, and Fused/GMS-backed location fail without Play Services. ## WakePoint — Background Sensor + Wakelock + Boot: the load-bearing recipe (API 24–36)

### The one thing that will kill this product if you get it wrong
A running **location foreground service does NOT keep the CPU awake** for a screen-off, backgrounded app. Default accelerometer/gyroscope are **non-wake-up sensors**: the HAL contract states they *"do not prevent the SoC from going into suspend mode"* and *"the drivers are not allowed to hold wake-locks."* When the SoC suspends, non-wake-up events go into a hardware FIFO and, if it overflows, *"the oldest data is dropped."* SensorManager will not save you — it only auto-holds a wake lock for wake-up sensors. **Your app must hold a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK for the entire ride.** ([suspend-mode](https://source.android.com/docs/core/interaction/sensors/suspend-mode))

### The edge case that makes the wakelock insufficient on its own: deep Doze
Doze's documented restrictions include *"Ignores wake locks."* Deep Doze engages when the device is unplugged, screen off, **and stationary**. A **sleeping rider's phone on a lap/seat/bag can go stationary mid-ride** — track vibration is frequently below the stationarity threshold. In deep Doze your PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK is ignored, the SoC suspends, and the sensor stream (and GPS) die. ([doze-standby](https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby))

The only OS-sanctioned escape: a **battery-optimization exemption**. *"An app that is partially exempt can use the network and hold partial wake locks during Doze and App Standby."* So the guaranteed recipe is **three things together**: location FGS (keeps process alive) + PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK (keeps CPU up) + battery-optimization exemption (keeps the wake lock honored in Doze). Drop any one and the 2 h screen-off promise breaks.

The lucky case: **Light Doze / "Doze on the go" (API 24+)** engages on a *moving* device and does **not** apply the full wake-lock restriction — so a genuinely moving train can survive on wakelock+FGS alone. But you cannot depend on continuous motion, so design for deep Doze. ([android-7.0-changes](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/nougat/android-7.0-changes))

### Sensor rate specifics
- WakePoint's 50–100 Hz is **below** the API 31 (Android 12) **200 Hz cap**, so **HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS is NOT required** and you will not hit the SecurityException. Only add it if you ever exceed 200 Hz. ([sensors_overview](https://developer.android.com/develop/sensors-and-location/sensors/sensors_overview))
- Register with **`maxReportLatencyUs = 0`** (no batching) for real-time between-GPS dead reckoning — which is exactly why the wake lock is mandatory (batching would let the SoC sleep). sensors_plus already uses zero batching; set samplingPeriod to ~10 ms (100 Hz) / ~20 ms (50 Hz). ([SensorManager](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/hardware/SensorManager))
- **Edge:** if the user turns off the **Microphone privacy toggle** (API 31+), motion sensors are throttled *regardless* of any permission. Measure the delivered rate at runtime and degrade gracefully.

### Foreground service type + boot (the dataSync trap)
On **Android 15 / API 35**, these FGS types are **blocked from BOOT_COMPLETED**: `dataSync`, `camera`, `mediaPlayback`, `phoneCall`, `mediaProjection` (`microphone` already blocked at API 34). **`location` is NOT restricted — a location FGS is still allowed from boot.** ([behavior-changes-15](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-15#fgs-boot-completed)) flutter_background_service can default to `dataSync`; that would be **blocked from boot and hit the 6 h cap** — you must force `foregroundServiceType="location"`. From API 34 you must also declare **FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION** and hold ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION. Your project's `targetSdk=34` means the API-35 boot rules are dormant today but activate the instant you bump to 35.

### Where to hold the wakelock in a flutter_background_service app (INFERENCE)
Acquire the PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK in **native Kotlin `onStartCommand`** of the foreground service, tied to service lifecycle, released in `onDestroy` — independent of the Dart background isolate's registration timing. Holding it via `wakelock_plus` from the isolate is possible but races on cold start; **never** hold it from the Activity/UI isolate (it dies when the Activity is destroyed with the screen off).

### Per-API-level manifest/permission recipe (guard with Build.VERSION.SDK_INT)
- **All (24–36):** `WAKE_LOCK`, `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`, `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`; native PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK; battery-optimization exemption gate before arming.
- **≥ 31 (Android 12):** stay ≤200 Hz (no HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS); handle mic-toggle throttling.
- **≥ 34 (Android 14):** add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`; `foregroundServiceType="location"`; `startForeground(..., FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_LOCATION)`; microphone FGS blocked from boot (irrelevant — you use location).
- **≥ 35 (Android 16 target, future):** keep `location` type (never `dataSync`); re-test boot path with `adb shell am compat enable FGS_BOOT_COMPLETED_RESTRICTIONS <pkg>`.

### India-first reality
Xiaomi/MIUI-HyperOS, Oppo/Realme/OnePlus-ColorOS, Vivo-FuntouchOS and Transsion (Tecno/Infinix/itel) disable **Autostart** by default and kill FGS + ignore battery-exemption more aggressively than AOSP. The AOSP permissions are necessary but **not sufficient** — ship OEM-detected onboarding deep-links to Autostart + "no battery restriction", and validate on real MIUI/ColorOS hardware with a 60–120 min stationary screen-off soak test. No-GMS devices: the sensor+wakelock+Doze path is pure AOSP and works, but geolocator's fused provider and google_maps_flutter need GMS fallbacks.

### HARD FACT vs INFERENCE summary
- HARD FACT (documented): non-wake-up suspend behavior; Doze ignores wake locks; exemption allows partial wake locks in Doze; light Doze (API 24) doesn't require stationarity; 200 Hz cap + HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS at API 31; mic-toggle throttling; FGS-from-boot restricted list at API 34/35 with `location` exempt; FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION at API 34; WAKE_LOCK is a normal permission; maxReportLatency batching semantics.
- INFERENCE: OEM autostart behavior; best place to hold the wakelock in the flutter_background_service isolate; Transsion low-memory process killing; no-GMS location fallbacks.

# WakePoint — Exact Alarms, Full-Screen Intent, Doze/Standby, Notifications/DND & Battery Exemption (API 24-36)

## Bottom line
WakePoint is a **genuine alarm-clock app**. That single fact unlocks the only combination that gives a *guaranteed, on-time, screen-off, Doze-proof* fire and is *Play-policy-permitted*:

- **`USE_EXACT_ALARM`** (API 33+, auto-granted, un-revokable, alarm-app only) instead of `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` (which is **denied by default on Android 14+**).
- **`AlarmManager.setAlarmClock()`** for the terminal fire (Doze-immune, not rate-limited, pierces every App Standby bucket).
- **`USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT`** (auto-granted for alarm apps on API 34+, guarded by `canUseFullScreenIntent()`).
- A dedicated **`IMPORTANCE_HIGH` channel with `USAGE_ALARM` audio** (rings through silent/vibrate) + optional **DND bypass**.
- **Avoid** `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` as a hard dependency (Play risk; unnecessary once the above are in place).

---

## 1. Exact alarms — the API-level story

| API | Change | HARD FACT |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | Doze introduced | Only `setAlarmClock`, `setAndAllowWhileIdle`, `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle` fire in Doze. The last two are capped at **once / 9 min / app**. `setAlarmClock` has no such cap and the system exits Doze just before it fires. |
| 31 | `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` special access | `setExact`/`setExactAndAllowWhileIdle`/`setAlarmClock` now need it or throw `SecurityException`. Auto-granted on 31-32 but **user-revokable**. Check `canScheduleExactAlarms()`. |
| 33 | `USE_EXACT_ALARM` normal permission | Auto-granted, **cannot be revoked**, full exact-alarm capability. **Play-restricted** to alarm/timer/calendar apps. |
| 34 | `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` **denied by default** | New installs targeting 33+ get it denied. **`USE_EXACT_ALARM` holders unaffected.** |

**Manifest (WakePoint):**
```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM"
    android:maxSdkVersion="32"/>
```

**Schedule guard:**
```kotlin
val am = context.getSystemService(AlarmManager::class.java)
if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.S || am.canScheduleExactAlarms()) {
    am.setAlarmClock(AlarmManager.AlarmClockInfo(triggerAtMillis, showIntent), opPi)
} else {
    context.startActivity(Intent(AlarmManager.ACTION_REQUEST_SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM)
        .setData(Uri.fromParts("package", context.packageName, null)))
}
```
With `USE_EXACT_ALARM` declared, `canScheduleExactAlarms()` is `true` on 33+ with no prompt.

> Why `setAlarmClock` and not `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle`: the latter is throttled to once/9-min in Doze and is a plain exact alarm subject to bucket limits; `setAlarmClock` is the OS's highest-priority alarm, exits Doze, and is the intended API for user-facing alarm clocks.

---

## 2. Doze & App Standby buckets

**Doze (API 23+):** screen-off + stationary + unplugged ⇒ network, jobs, syncs, wakelocks, standard alarms deferred to maintenance windows. High-priority alarms (above) pierce it.

**Buckets (API 28+) — alarm limits (HARD FACT, power-management table):**

| Bucket | Alarm limit | Network |
|---|---|---|
| Active | none | full |
| Working set | 10/hr | full |
| Frequent | 2/hr | full |
| Rare | 1/hr | **off** |
| Restricted (API 31+) | **1/day** (exact or inexact) | **off** |

**Key exemption (HARD FACT):** apps holding **`USE_EXACT_ALARM`** are **exempt from the Restricted bucket** entirely. Restricted threshold: 45 days idle (API 31-32) → 8 days idle (API 33+). During an actual ride WakePoint is in active/working-set anyway (foreground service + user interaction), and `setAlarmClock` is not throttled regardless — buckets are effectively a non-issue for the fire itself.

---

## 3. Full-screen intent (the "wake the rider over the lock screen" mechanism)

| API | Behavior (HARD FACT) |
|---|---|
| 29-33 | `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT` is a normal, auto-granted permission. FSI launches full-screen over lock screen. |
| 34 | Becomes a **special app-access appop**. Only **alarm/calling** apps auto-granted; Play revokes the default for others (enforced **Jan 22 2025**). Check `canUseFullScreenIntent()`; send users to `ACTION_MANAGE_APP_USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT`. |
| 35 | Same rule reaffirmed. |
| 36 | Apps targeting 16 must explicitly declare the permission; alarm category still auto-granted. |

**AOSP screen-state table (HARD FACT):** when **granted**, FSI launches full-screen in **every** state — unlocked, locked, screen-off, always-on-display. When **denied**, it degrades to a 60-second heads-up notification. This is exactly WakePoint's screen-off scenario, so a *granted* FSI is a genuine full-screen wake.

**Guard:**
```kotlin
val nm = context.getSystemService(NotificationManager::class.java)
val canFsi = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < 34 || nm.canUseFullScreenIntent()
val b = Notification.Builder(context, WAKE_CHANNEL)
    .setCategory(Notification.CATEGORY_ALARM)
    .setFullScreenIntent(alarmActivityPi, true)  // ignored gracefully if not permitted
// if !canFsi: also start ACTION_MANAGE_APP_USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT and rely on
// IMPORTANCE_HIGH heads-up + looping USAGE_ALARM audio as the fallback.
```
**Play Console:** App content → declare `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT` with **alarm** core functionality (required since **May 31 2024**).

---

## 4. Notification channel, alarm audio, ringer & DND

- **Channels (API 26+):** importance/sound/bypass are **immutable after creation**. Create one dedicated `wake_alarm_v1` channel: `IMPORTANCE_HIGH`, `CATEGORY_ALARM` on the notification.
- **Ring through silent/vibrate (HARD FACT):** set the channel sound with `AudioAttributes` `USAGE_ALARM` + `CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION`. Alarm-stream audio is independent of the ringer, so it plays in silent/vibrate. (Raise/verify `STREAM_ALARM` volume; don't touch the ringer.)
- **DND bypass (best-effort):** `channel.setBypassDnd(true)` only works if the app holds **`ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY`**, which the **user must grant** via `ACTION_NOTIFICATION_POLICY_ACCESS_SETTINGS` (check `isNotificationPolicyAccessGranted()`). Prompt during onboarding; treat denial as non-fatal.

```kotlin
val attrs = AudioAttributes.Builder()
    .setUsage(AudioAttributes.USAGE_ALARM)
    .setContentType(AudioAttributes.CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION).build()
val ch = NotificationChannel("wake_alarm_v1", "Wake-up alarm", NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_HIGH)
ch.setSound(alarmUri, attrs)
ch.setBypassDnd(true)   // effective only with ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY granted
```
Also declare **`POST_NOTIFICATIONS`** (runtime permission, API 33+).

---

## 5. Battery-optimization exemption — use carefully

- `ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` (direct-grant dialog) is **Play-policy restricted**; alarm clocks are **not** on the acceptable-use list, and Google's position is that a correct exact-alarm app **doesn't need it** because `USE_EXACT_ALARM` + `setAlarmClock` already pierce Doze.
- The **non-restricted** `ACTION_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATION_SETTINGS` (opens the full list) is allowed for any app.
- **WakePoint nuance:** the *alarm* doesn't need exemption, but the **2-hour continuous location foreground service + 50-100Hz sensor stream** is exactly what aggressive OEMs kill. So request exemption/autostart **framed around the foreground service**, via the non-restricted path, not as an alarm requirement.

---

## 6. Resilience architecture (belt & suspenders)
1. **Location foreground service** (`FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`, API 34) for proximity.
2. **Pre-armed `setAlarmClock`** at ride start — survives process death (lives in system AlarmManager, not your process). This is the single most important reliability decision for cheap/aggressive-OEM/no-GMS phones.
3. **At fire time:** FSI + `IMPORTANCE_HIGH` heads-up + looping `USAGE_ALARM` audio + DND bypass.
4. On no-GMS devices there is **no FCM re-wake** — so (2) must not depend on any network.

---

### 3. PER-DEVICE-CLASS capability statement (for founder → users/investors)

- **Mainstream Android (Pixel / recent Samsung / stock) — FULLY.** Wakes reliably with only standard permission prompts. The no-timeout location service + Doze-piercing `setAlarmClock` deliver the 2h screen-off guarantee. *Samsung caveat:* add WakePoint to "Never sleeping apps" so live tracking survives (the alarm fires either way).
- **Aggressive-OEM Android (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, Realme, OnePlus, Transsion) — WITH_SETUP.** The dominant India class and the top product-death risk. The pre-armed system alarm still rings, but the live tracking service is killed unless the user enables **Autostart**, sets battery to **Unrestricted**, and **locks the app in recents** — driven by an in-app OEM onboarding wizard. Honest limit: some firmware ignores even these; the system-level pre-armed alarm is the safety net.
- **Android Go / low-RAM (2GB) — WITH_SETUP.** Memory pressure kills the service; the pre-armed `setAlarmClock` (in system AlarmManager, not the app process) is the anchor. Needs battery exemption, a lightweight throttled/batched service, and a persistent notification. Live accuracy degrades; the wake is preserved.
- **No-gyroscope phones — DEGRADED.** Still wakes the rider via GPS + accelerometer + alarm; loses gyro-fused precision between fixes (tunnels, tight stops). App detects gyro absence and widens the safety margin (wakes slightly earlier).
- **Huawei/Honor & no-GMS/AOSP — DEGRADED.** The entire wake path works **offline** (exact alarm, sensors, location FGS, alarm audio, vibration, full-screen intent). Maps, Places, Ads, IAP, fused location, and FCM re-wake all fail — require raw LocationManager + bundled OSM assets + disabled monetization, all kept off the alarm-critical path. Some forks pre-deny exact alarms; verify on-device.
- **iOS — UNSUPPORTED (honest, un-closable for this architecture).** iOS gives no equivalent to a long-lived location foreground service + partial wake lock + high-rate background IMU + arbitrary alarm audio from a suspended app. A reduced iOS product (region monitoring, significant-location-change, critical-alert local notifications needing Apple approval) is possible but cannot make the same on-time screen-off promise. Scope separately or defer; do not represent it as feature-parity.
